nodes.Name: ryuFtoaFixed32
nodes.DocComment: ryuFtoaFixed32 formats mant*(2^exp) with prec decimal digits.

nodes.Name: ryuFtoaFixed64
nodes.DocComment: ryuFtoaFixed64 formats mant*(2^exp) with prec decimal digits.

nodes.Name: formatDecimal
nodes.DocComment:
formatDecimal fills d with at most prec decimal digits
of mantissa m. The boolean trunc indicates whether m
is truncated compared to the original number being formatted.

nodes.Name: ryuFtoaShortest
nodes.DocComment: ryuFtoaShortest formats mant*2^exp with prec decimal digits.

nodes.Name: mulByLog2Log10
nodes.DocComment:
mulByLog2Log10 returns math.Floor(x * log(2)/log(10)) for an integer x in
the range -1600 <= x && x <= +1600.

The range restriction lets us work in faster integer arithmetic instead of
slower floating point arithmetic. Correctness is verified by unit tests.

nodes.Name: mulByLog10Log2
nodes.DocComment:
mulByLog10Log2 returns math.Floor(x * log(10)/log(2)) for an integer x in
the range -500 <= x && x <= +500.

The range restriction lets us work in faster integer arithmetic instead of
slower floating point arithmetic. Correctness is verified by unit tests.

nodes.Name: computeBounds
nodes.DocComment:
computeBounds returns a floating-point vector (l, c, u)×2^e2
where the mantissas are 55-bit (or 26-bit) integers, describing the interval
represented by the input float64 or float32.

nodes.Name: ryuDigits32
nodes.DocComment: ryuDigits32 emits decimal digits for a number less than 1e9.

nodes.Name: mult64bitPow10
nodes.DocComment:
mult64bitPow10 takes a floating-point input with a 25-bit
mantissa and multiplies it with 10^q. The resulting mantissa
is m*P >> 57 where P is a 64-bit element of the detailedPowersOfTen tables.
It is typically 31 or 32-bit wide.
The returned boolean is true if all trimmed bits were zero.

That is:

	m*2^e2 * round(10^q) = resM * 2^resE + ε
	exact = ε == 0

nodes.Name: mult128bitPow10
nodes.DocComment:
mult128bitPow10 takes a floating-point input with a 55-bit
mantissa and multiplies it with 10^q. The resulting mantissa
is m*P >> 119 where P is a 128-bit element of the detailedPowersOfTen tables.
It is typically 63 or 64-bit wide.
The returned boolean is true is all trimmed bits were zero.

That is:

	m*2^e2 * round(10^q) = resM * 2^resE + ε
	exact = ε == 0

nodes.Name: divmod1e9
nodes.DocComment:
divmod1e9 computes quotient and remainder of division by 1e9,
avoiding runtime uint64 division on 32-bit platforms.
